title: Budget App
description: Build a budget application that tracks expenses by category, monitors spending limits, and generates monthly reports.

steps.title: Define budget categories with limits
steps.description: Create a `budgetCategories` array with objects containing `id`, `name`, and `limit` (max spending per month). Also create an empty `expenses` array. Log the categories.
hints: Create 4 categories: food, transportation, entertainment, utilities
Log both the categories and empty expenses array

codeTemplate.python:
import json

budgetCategories = [
  {"id": "food", "name": "Food & Dining", "limit": 500},
  {"id": "transport", "name": "Transportation", "limit": 200},
  {"id": "entertainment", "name": "Entertainment", "limit": 150},
  {"id": "utilities", "name": "Utilities", "limit": 300}
]

expenses = []

print(json.dumps(budgetCategories))
print("Expenses count:", len(expenses))

verification.successMessage: Budget categories with limits and expenses array are initialized!
verification.failureMessage: Create at least 4 budget categories with id, name, and limit fields, plus an empty expenses array.

steps.title: Implement addExpense function
steps.description: Write an `addExpense` function that takes `categoryId`, `amount`, `date`, and `description`. Creates an expense object with a unique id and appends it to the expenses array. Log the new expense.
hints: Create expense: { id: nextId, categoryId, amount, date, description }
Use expenses.push(newExpense) to add, then log the new expense

verification.successMessage: Expenses can be added with all required fields!
verification.failureMessage: addExpense should create an expense object with id, categoryId, amount, date, and description, then add it to the expenses array.

steps.title: Calculate spending by category
steps.description: Write a `getCategorySpending` function that takes a `categoryId` and returns the total amount spent in that category. Log the total for food.
hints: Filter expenses by categoryId: expenses.filter(e => e.categoryId === categoryId)
Sum the amounts: .reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.amount, 0) or loop
Return the total (rounded to 2 decimal places)

verification.successMessage: Category spending calculates the correct totals!
verification.failureMessage: getCategorySpending('food') should return 57.5 (45.50 + 12.00). getCategorySpending('transport') should return 30.

steps.title: Check budget alerts
steps.description: Write a `checkBudgetAlerts` function that returns an array of categories where spending has exceeded the limit. Log the alerts.
hints: For each category, get its spending and compare to its limit
If spending > limit, include: { id, name, spent, limit, overBy }

verification.successMessage: Budget alerts detect categories that exceed their limits!
verification.failureMessage: checkBudgetAlerts should return an array with 'food' overspent by $10 (spent $60, limit $50).

steps.title: Generate monthly budget report
steps.description: Write a `monthlyReport` function that takes a `month` and `year`, and returns a formatted string with each category's spending, limit, remaining, and alert status.
hints: Filter expenses by date: e.date.startsWith(year + '-' + month)
Add '[OVER]' or '[OK]' tag based on whether limit is exceeded

verification.successMessage: Monthly report shows category breakdown with over-budget alerts!
verification.failureMessage: monthlyReport should show 'Food & Dining: $300 / $500 ($200 remaining) [OK]' and 'Entertainment: $200 / $150 ($-50 remaining) [OVER]'.
